# Variable selection, run end to end

*Generated by `creditsurv select`. Every number comes from this run.*

## What was run

Steps 5 to 9 of `docs/variable_selection.md`, on the training half of the whole
population up to 2021-12, under the `exclude` moratorium policy:
**72,671,500 cells covering 2,112,532,468 loan-months**, with no sampling
at any step.

Two departures from the first run, both to keep the backtest honest. The selection sees
only the training half, because a specification chosen on the months the model is judged
on has already seen the test. And stability is judged across loans originated in even and
in odd years -- two halves that each cover every calendar month -- rather than across the
whole population and its first 94%, which needs the test window.

## Chosen

`C(credit_score, Treatment(790.0)) + C(original_ltv, Treatment(50.0)) + C(debt_to_income, Treatment(19.0)) + term_years + moratorium_regime + ltv_change + unemployment_change + financial_conditions + consumer_sentiment + C(purpose, Treatment('purchase')) + C(occupancy, Treatment('owner_occupied')) + C(harp, Treatment('standard')) + C(mortgage_insurance, Treatment('uninsured'))`

| Equity volatility | step 8: wrong sign: +0.001257 where - is expected |
| House price growth | step 8: wrong sign: -0.7799 where + is expected |
| Housing starts growth | step 9: 1 sd effect +0.040 on even vintages, +0.044 on odd vintages, +0.046 on to 2010 06, -0.003 on after 2010 06, beside ltv_change (-0.201), both housing |
| Mortgage rate fall since origination | step 8: wrong sign: -0.1572 where + is expected |
| Volatility change since origination | step 8: wrong sign: +0.0004447 where - is expected |

### 9. Stability

### 10. Materiality

A macro covariate whose effect of one standard deviation on log survival time is under
0.02 in absolute value contributes its sign and little else, and a covariate
that small changes sign when the sample does. The threshold is fixed in `docs/rules.md`,
before any of these fits, and the removals are made one at a time because each one moves
every other coefficient.

Every covariate that survived step 9 clears the threshold.
